Senior Developer Engineer You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Story ticket ready for development]) --> READ_INPUT["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ_INPUT --> PARENT["Read parent epic context if present:
- input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md — business rules
- input/TICKET/parent_context_sa.md — technical design
- input/TICKET/parent_context_vd.md — visual design"] PARENT --> ANALYZE["Analyze requirements — every acceptance criterion must be addressed"] ANALYZE --> ARCH["Understand existing codebase patterns, architecture, and test structure"] ARCH --> PRINCIPLES["Apply OOP principles: SRP, OCP, DI, Encapsulation, Composition over inheritance"] PRINCIPLES --> TDD["Follow TDD approach — see tdd_approach.md"] TDD --> TEST_LOC["Write TDD tests in the standard unit-test tree only
— Flutter/Dart: test/
— NEVER in testing/ (owned by test-automation agents)"] TEST_LOC --> IMPLEMENT["Implement source code and unit tests following existing patterns"] IMPLEMENT --> DOCS["Update documentation ONLY if ticket explicitly requires it"] DOCS --> RUN["Run all unit tests — MUST pass before finishing"] RUN --> PASS{Tests pass?} PASS -->|No| FIX["Fix failures and re-run tests"] FIX --> RUN PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise PR description to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles branch, commit and PR]) ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD — Test-Driven Development Workflow"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the requirement"] T1["RED: Write a failing unit test FIRST
— before any production code
— test must describe the expected behavior
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum production code to make the test PASS
— no over-engineering
— simplest possible implementation"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up code while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— apply OOP principles
— run tests after every change"] T4{"More requirements to implement?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next behavior"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All behaviors implemented with tests]) end subgraph RULES["TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER write production code without a failing test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more production code than needed to pass the test"] R3["✅ Tests must be fast, isolated, and deterministic"] R4["✅ Aim for 100% unit test coverage on new and modified code"] R5["✅ When behavior involves a loop/collection, add a case with 2+ items, not only a single-item happy path — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still wrong"] R6["✅ Run the full test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## Where to write TDD tests Write failing unit / widget tests in the project's standard unit-test tree **only**: - Flutter / Dart projects → `test/` - Node projects → `__tests__/` or `test/` according to the repo convention - Python projects → `tests/` or project-specific unit-test directory ❌ **Never** place development TDD tests under `testing/`. `testing/` is owned by test-automation agents (regression probes, workflow observation tests, accessibility gates, etc.). If your production changes break existing tests there, leave them untouched and mention the breakage in `outputs/response.md` so the test-automation agent can update them. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/response.md — concise PR description"] O2["Target length: under 20 lines. A reviewer should understand the change in under 30 seconds"] O3["Required sections:
### What changed
1-2 sentences describing the implementation"] O4["### Key decisions
Bullet list of architectural or design choices"] O5["### How to verify
Test command or verification steps"] O6["Optional: add a mermaid diagram inside <details> block summarizing the change"] O7["❌ NO verbose restatement of ticket requirements
❌ NO water words or filler text"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 --> O7 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md is a PR description — not a report or essay"] F2["Use bullet points and short sentences, not paragraphs"] F3["Technical focus: WHAT changed and WHY, not WHAT the ticket asked for"] F4["If including mermaid diagram: wrap in <details><summary>Architecture</summary>...</details>"] ``` Example PR descriptions — follow this structure and brevity: ```mermaid flowchart TD E1["### What changed
Added JWT validation interceptor to protect all authenticated endpoints."] E2["### Key decisions
- Reused existing `AuthFilter` pattern instead of introducing Spring Security
- Extracted token validation into `JwtValidator` service for testability and reuse"] E3["### How to verify
```bash
./gradlew test --tests '*AuthInterceptorTest*'
```"] E4["<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
REQ[HTTP Request] --> INT[AuthInterceptor]
INT --> VAL[JwtValidator]
VAL -->|valid| CTL[Controller]
VAL -->|invalid| ERR[401 Response]
```

</details>"] ``` ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SAFETY["CLI command safety"] S1["One simple executable command at a time"] S2["DMTools rejects shell metacharacters"] end subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"] F1["Pipes: |"] F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"] F3["Chaining: ; && ||"] F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"] end subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"] E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."] E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"] E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end USE --> SAFETY SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN SAFETY --> EXAMPLES SAFETY --> CWD ```

Machine comments on GitHub issues use Jira wiki markup ({code}, h3.) — engage cliPromptsByTracker for github (markdown) + wire trackerType in CliAgent
## Summary

Machine comments on GitHub issues are posted in **Jira wiki markup** (observed on #122: 6× `{code}` blocks, 4× `h3.` headers — unreadable on GitHub). The ecosystem has a per-tracker formatting mechanism, but it is never engaged for our GitHub loop:

1. `cliPromptsByTracker` exists (`agents/intake.json`): `{"jira": [jira_markup_transform.md, jira_comment_format.md], "ado": [ado_markup_transform.md, ado_comment_format.md]}` — but **bug/story development configs don't set it at all**, and there is **no `github` key** / no `agents/instructions/tracker/github_comment_format.md` upstream.
2. The Dart port never passes `trackerType` into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands` (`lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart:249-255` calls it without the arg) — `resolveCliPrompts` then defaults to `"ado"`, so even a `github` key would never be selected. Java passes the tracker type from the job/ticket context.

## Evidence (gh-122 machine comments)

```
{code}dart
final reader = PropertyReader();
{code}
h3. Fix
```

## Fix (machine-kit side first — no upstream wait)

1. Add `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md`: markdown rules — fenced ``` blocks, `##`/`###` headers, no `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables.
2. Wire into runners `machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/fa-*.json` (dev + rework): `"cliPromptsByTracker": {"github": ["./machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md"]}` (config_merger deep-merges the map with the parent).
3. Dart parity fix: pass `trackerType` into `buildCommands`, derived from the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader — `github` when the GitHub router serves the ticket) so the `github` key resolves. (Java `CliCommandBuilder` receives the tracker from the ticket context.)
4. Upstream (dmtools-agents PR, later): add `github` entries to dev configs + share the markdown format file.

## Impact

Readability of every machine comment on GitHub issues (#122, #123, and all future runs).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Jira tracker comment

Use Jira wiki markup in `outputs/response.md`.

- Headings: `h1.`, `h2.`, `h3.`
- Bullets: `* item`
- Numbered lists: `# item`
- Bold: `*text*`
- Inline code: `{{code}}`
- Code block: `{code}...{code}`
- Link: `[title|url]`

Do not use Markdown headings, fenced code blocks, or backtick inline code.

**IMPORTANT** When answering a clarification question about a user story, get the parent story for full context using: `dmtools jira_get_ticket PARENT-KEY` (the parent key is visible in the ticket's parent field).

content.text:
Every integration dmtools exposes belongs to one of two unified abstractions.
Agent scripts, job configs, and the port itself must be written against the
abstraction — never against a concrete vendor.

### 1. Tracker — any work-tracking system

Jira, ADO Boards, GitHub Issues, Rally, … — one interface:
`tracker_get_ticket`, `tracker_search`, `tracker_post_comment`,
`tracker_move_to_status`, `tracker_add_label`, … Every concrete
`jira_*` / `ado_*` / `github_*` issue tool is an implementation of the same
contract, and the `tracker_*` surface must route to whichever tracker the
environment configures (`DEFAULT_TRACKER`). A script written against
`params.ticket.key` + tracker tools must run unchanged on any tracker
backend. Context hydration follows the same contract: `params.ticket` /
`params.ticketKey` carry the ticket key and data regardless of vendor.

### 2. SCM — any source-control system

GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, ADO Repos, … — one interface for PR / branch /
commit / review operations (the `js/common/scm.js` provider abstraction in
the agent ecosystem; `github_*` / `gitlab_*` / `bitbucket_*` sync tools
underneath). Review, rework, and development flows must be SCM-agnostic:
ticket → PR → review → rework → merge works the same regardless of vendor.

### Consequences

- **Porting rule:** a vendor integration is "done" only when its tools are
  reachable through the unified interface (tracker routing, SCM providers) —

Machine comments on GitHub issues are posted in **Jira wiki markup** (observed on #122: 6× `{code}` blocks, 4× `h3.` headers — unreadable on GitHub). The ecosystem has a per-tracker formatting mechanism, but it is never engaged for our GitHub loop:

The Dart port never passes `trackerType` into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands` (`lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart:249-255` calls it without the arg) — `resolveCliPrompts` then defaults to `"ado"`, so even a `github` key would never be selected. Java passes the tracker type from the job/ticket context.

## Evidence (gh-122 machine comments)

```
{code}dart
final reader = PropertyReader();
{code}
h3. Fix
```

## Fix (machine-kit side first — no upstream wait)

1. Add `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md`: markdown rules — fenced ``` blocks, `##`/`###` headers, no `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables.
2. Wire into runners `machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/fa-*.json` (dev + rework): `"cliPromptsByTracker": {"github": ["./machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md"]}` (config_merger deep-merges the map with the parent).

4. Upstream (dmtools-agents PR, later): add `github` entries to dev configs + share the markdown format file.

## Impact

# dmtools.env.example — machine-kit/teammate-install (committed template)
# Copy to dmtools.env (git-ignored, same dir) and fill the keys.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Provider: z.ai (fa catalog kind "zai" — the CODING plan endpoint).
# FILL ME: set ZAI_API_KEY below — everything else is ready.
# (install-dmtools-fa.json → install.sh sources this file; the real
# environment still wins. This file is git-ignored.)

# ── 1. dmtools-dart CLI (Dart orchestrator, epam/dmtools-dart) ──────
DMTOOLS_DART_VERSION=latest
# Side-by-side with the Java CLI — never clobbers ~/.dmtools.
DMTOOLS_DART_INSTALL_DIR="${HOME}/.dmtools-dart"

# ── 2. fa CLI (agent harness, IstiN/flutter_agent_harness) ──────────
FA_VERSION=latest
FA_INSTALL_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin"

# ── 3. Workflow-level key separation ────────────────────────────────
# Each runner job (machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/*.json) inherits a
# dmtools-agents agent and overrides ONLY the env variables — including
# WHICH key it uses, via FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG.apiKeyEnvVar. This file holds
# the values under workflow-scoped names; job override > dmtools.env, so
# a workflow always runs with its own key.

# runners/fa-code-zai.json (code → z.ai glm-5.3-flash):
ZAI_CODE_KEY=__FILL_ME__

# runners/fa-review-kimi.json (review → Kimi kimi-k3-256k):
KIMI_REVIEW_KEY=__FILL_ME__

# Shared fallbacks for MANUAL fa runs (no workflow binding):
#   ZAI_API_KEY=__FILL_ME__    KIMI_API_KEY=__FILL_ME__

# ── 4. Default provider for MANUAL fa runs (no job override) ────────
FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_API_KEY"}'

echo "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted — served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper>/'
          else
            echo "::error::dry-run credential was NOT served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper — a github.com push would not authenticate as the SOURCE account"
            printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted>/'
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          # fa provider contract (env preconfig; the runner JSON also pins
          # these via params.envVariables — job env beats it, this step env
          # matches it. Keys: workflow-level separation, same names as
          # machine-kit/teammate-install/dmtools.env).
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          # fa session identity (run-agent.sh -> fa-session.sh): deterministic
          # name fa-<repo>-gh-<n>-<group>-<hash8>, resume-or-create; the cache
          # steps carry it across CI runs.
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh operations inside the session (pr create/edit, api, …) must act
          # AS the SOURCE account: events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not
          # trigger workflows, and commits/PRs created via the API author as
          # github-actions[bot]. Same PAT-first fallback as auto-update-prs.yml.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          # FULL session trace: run-agent.sh passes FA_LOG_FILE to
          # `fa --log-file` (fa >= v0.1.335, flutter_agent_harness#91),
          # which tees every line fa prints — assistant text and tool
          # calls, untruncated — to the file, uploaded as an artifact
          # below. dmtools mirrors child output live to its own stderr
          # (gh-50), so the agent's work already streams into this step's
          # log as it happens; the follower side-channel is gone.
          FA_LOG_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          export FA_LOG_FILE
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
          touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          echo "fa full trace: ${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          # Capture the run output for the verdict step below: the final
          # dmtools result is a JSON blob ({"success":…,"results":[{
          # "response":"# PR … verdict: …"}]}) — tee keeps it visible in
          # the step log AND on disk for `Apply the review verdict`.
          RUN_OUTPUT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/run-output.txt"
          dmtools run "${RUNNER}" \
            --metadata '{"contextId":"gh-${{ github.event.issue.number }}"}' \
            --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}" --debug 2>&1 | tee "${RUN_OUTPUT}"
          RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          exit "${RC}"

      - name: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)
        # Zero-maintainer keystone: convert the review agent's verdict into
        # the label that drives the next machine step — nobody reads logs.
        #   APPROVE (+ green CI on the PR head) → pr_approved on the issue →
        #     merge-trigger.yml picks it up and squash-merges the linked PR.
        #   CHANGES_REQUESTED / BLOCK           → agent:rework on the issue →
        #     the labeled event re-fires this workflow with the rework runner.

I see. The workflow doesn't set `DEFAULT_TRACKER` explicitly. But the ticket says "derived from the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader — `github` when the GitHub router serves the ticket)".

The key phrase: "`github` when the GitHub router serves the ticket". In the Dart port, the GitHub router serves the ticket when `looksLikeGithubQuery(inputJql)` is true in TeammateJob. So perhaps the fix is:
1. In `TeammateJob`, when `github` is true (GitHub router serves the tickets), pass `trackerType: 'github'` to the `CliAgent` (or set DEFAULT_TRACKER override).
2. In `CliAgent._executeCliCommands`, pass `propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` as `trackerType` to `buildCommands`.

Actually the cleanest parity approach: Java's `CliCommandBuilder` receives `configuration` (TrackerConfiguration) and calls `configuration.getDefaultTracker()` directly inside `buildCommands`. The Dart `buildCommands` can't access PropertyReader (it's a const class with pure functions). The ticket says "pass `trackerType` into `buildCommands`, derived from the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader...)" — i.e., in `cli_agent.dart`, compute `propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` and pass it.

But then "github when the GitHub router serves the ticket" — if DEFAULT_TRACKER isn't set anywhere in the ai-teammate env, the lookup returns null → falls back to "ado" → github key never resolves. Hmm.

Wait — let me check `TeammateJob._runSingle` for the pass-through path and `_githubCommentPoster`. Also check if `TeammateJob` sets any env overrides. Let me look at the whole teammate_job.dart to understand what happens for the pass-through path (inputJql empty — the ai-teammate issue-trigger loop passes `inputJql: ""` in the runner configs and prepares `input/ticket.md`).

In the runners (fa-bug-dev.json etc.), `inputJql: ""` → pass-through path: `_preparedInputTicket()` reads the prepared input and runs one CliAgent with a synthetic ticket. In this path, `_sourceIsGithub` stays false. Hmm.

So how does "the GitHub router serves the ticket" manifest in the Dart code? Let me look at `_preparedInputTicket` and the surrounding logic.

- name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          # ticket.json carries the tracker-contract fields (key/number/
          # title/body/labels): dmtools hydrates it into params.ticket for
          # every JS action (GOAL.md → Core abstractions → Tracker), so
          # scripts read params.ticket.key exactly like on a Jira machine.
          mkdir -p "input/gh-${NUMBER}"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("gh-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"
          echo "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json: $(wc -c < input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json) bytes"

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.
        # What each section proves:
        #   --show-origin        WHERE each credential source lives; the
        #                        extraheader section must come back empty —
        #                        asserted below, so any resurrection of the
        #                        App-token header (checkout layout change,
        #                        mid-run config write) fails the run here
        #                        instead of silently re-arming bot pushes
        #   submodule foreach    same proof for each submodule local config
        #                        (checkout arms those with submodules: true)
        #   git credential fill  dry-runs the exact push-path resolution and
        #                        shows the winning username; the password is
        #                        masked, and the helper's stderr line confirms
        #                        SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN served the credential
        env:

        run: |
          mkdir -p .dmtools
          echo "── credential.helper — all scopes, with origins ──"
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper || true
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper || true
          echo "── http.https://github.com/.extraheader (must be empty — App token purged) ──"
          # Redact the VALUE (gh-63 review threads 11/12): on a leftover this
          # dump prints AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)> — GitHub's
          # log masking matches the raw token string, not its base64 form.
          # git 2.x prints "<origin>\t<value>" (--show-origin --get-all has
          # NO key= prefix), so redact everything after the first TAB — a
          # sed on '=' alone would only trim the base64 padding. The origin
          # (file/scope) stays visible; a tab-less line is fully redacted.
          git config --show-origin --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader | sed -E 's/^([^\t]*\t).*/\1<redacted>/; t; s/.+/<redacted> (unexpected line without origin)/' || true

          # checkout arms every submodule's local config with the same token;
          # a push made from inside agents/ must not fall back to it (gh-63).
          # The probe echoes a LEFTOVER marker line only when a config is
          # still armed, so "no submodules" and "all clean" stay quiet.
          # The marker names the submodule but NEVER the header value: it is
          # AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)>, decodable and NOT masked
          # by GitHub log redaction (gh-63 review threads 11/12).
          sub_leftovers="$(git submodule foreach --quiet --recursive \
            'c="$(git config --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true)"; [ -z "$c" ] || echo "LEFTOVER ${sm_path}: <redacted>"' \
            || true)"
          if [ -n "$sub_leftovers" ]; then
            echo "::error::App-token extraheader still present in a submodule config after purge — pushes from inside the submodule would authenticate as github-actions[bot]"
            printf '%s\n' "$sub_leftovers"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "── commit identity ──"
          git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT
          git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT

          # fill` exits 0 even when NO helper answered (echo prints its prompt

          # SOURCE helper's username proves the SOURCE credential wins.
          # CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tags the helper's log line so this dry-run
          # stays distinguishable from real pushes in the evidence log.

          if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^username=x-access-token$'; then
            echo "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted — served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper>/'

"derived from the active tracker (DEFAULT_TRACKER via PropertyReader …)" — the derivation mechanism IS `DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader. The em-dash clause "— github when the GitHub router serves the ticket" explains under which condition the value is github.

Two readings:
A. Code derives: `trackerType = propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()`; deployment sets DEFAULT_TRACKER=github when GitHub serves the tickets.
B. Code derives from the router: `trackerType = sourceIsGithub ? 'github' : propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()`.

Java reality: `buildCommands` uses ONLY `configuration.getDefaultTracker()` (plus the confluence contentOutput override). On a Java machine serving GitHub tickets... wait, does Java even support GitHub tickets as Teammate input? Java Teammate uses JQL against Jira/ADO. The GitHub-issues loop is this repo's own extension (dart-side github_ticket_source). So "the Java source is the spec" → mechanism = getDefaultTracker() only (reading A).

But then the deployment MUST set DEFAULT_TRACKER=github for the fix to engage. Where? The runners' envVariables is the committed place — job env beats dmtools.env, so it's deterministic. I'll add `"DEFAULT_TRACKER": "github"` to the dev + rework runner envVariables and document why in the PR description.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider B vs A once more, looking at the Java ticket context mention: "(Java `CliCommandBuilder` receives the tracker from the ticket context.)" — In Java, `configuration.getDefaultTracker()`... `configuration` here is the DMToolsConfiguration injected into CliCommandBuilder. That IS "the tracker from the job context" (configuration = the app-level config). OK so Java = getDefaultTracker(). Reading A. Good — and to make it actually resolve to github, set DEFAULT_TRACKER=github in the runner env (this deployment's active tracker is GitHub).

Decision (final):
- Dart: `_executeCliCommands` passes `trackerType: propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` (exact Java parity — Java computes it inside buildCommands from configuration; Dart passes it in since CliCommandBuilder is a pure const class; the ticket explicitly says "pass trackerType into buildCommands").
- Runners: wire cliPromptsByTracker.github (ticket step 2) + DEFAULT_TRACKER=github in envVariables (ticket step 3's "github when the GitHub router serves the ticket" made real for this GitHub-issues loop).

Wait, one more consideration on setting DEFAULT_TRACKER=github in envVariables: it changes `tracker_*` alias routing for any `dmtools` CLI calls the agent makes inside the session (envVariables flow into the subprocess env — let me verify `_buildSubprocessEnvironment`). If the agent calls `tracker_post_comment`, with DEFAULT_TRACKER=github it routes to `github_create_comment` — correct for this loop (comments land on the GitHub issue). Without it, aliases would silently hit Jira (the known gh-35 parity bug). So it's a strict improvement for this deployment and consistent with "a script written against the abstraction must run unchanged on any tracker backend".

# ADO tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for Azure DevOps work item comments and descriptions.

- Headings: `#`, `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item` or `* item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` `
- Link: `[title](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax

Do not use Jira wiki markup (`h1.`, `*text*`, `{code}`, `[title|url]`) in ADO fields.

**IMPORTANT** When answering a clarification question about a user story, get the parent story for full context using: `dmtools ado_get_work_item PARENT-KEY` (the parent key is visible in the ticket's parent field).

**IMPORTANT** When enhancing story descriptions, check child tickets and parent story for better context using: `dmtools ado_search_by_wiql`.

**Step 1 (RED)**: Add lifecycle tests in `test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart`:
- `lifecycleTrackerPromptsTests()`:
  1. `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github` env override → github prompts merged into the command prompt (via `cat` trick).
  2. No DEFAULT_TRACKER → falls back to 'ado' behavior (ado prompts merged, github not).
  3. DEFAULT_TRACKER=jira → jira prompts merged.

Run → confirm fail (trackerType currently never passed → always 'ado').

**Step 2 (GREEN)**: `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart` — `_executeCliCommands` passes `trackerType: propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()`.

**Step 3 (machine-kit wiring tests RED)**: New test group in `test/machine_kit/` (maybe `tracker_prompts_wiring_test.dart`) asserting:
- resolved `fa-bug-dev.json` params.cliPromptsByTracker['github'] contains the format file path
- same for fa-story-dev.json, fa-rework-zai.json
- format file exists on disk
- runner envVariables pin DEFAULT_TRACKER=github (if I decide to add it — YES, needed for the github key to actually resolve; document it)

**Step 4 (GREEN)**: Create `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md` + wire runners.

Wait — regarding DEFAULT_TRACKER=github in the runners: let me think about side effects once more. envVariables are also the PropertyReader overrides for the whole job run. `getDefaultTracker()` is used by:
1. `_executeCliCommands` (my new code) — wants github ✓
2. `cli_dispatcher` alias resolution — for `dmtools tracker_*` calls made by the agent inside the session... wait, the agent subprocess env gets DEFAULT_TRACKER=github too (via _buildSubprocessEnvironment → PropertyReader.getOverrides()). When the agent invokes `dmtools tracker_get_ticket`, cli_dispatcher reads `_env['DEFAULT_TRACKER']` — where `_env` is... let me check what `_env` is in cli_dispatcher — likely Platform.environment. So the subprocess env → `dmtools tracker_*` routes to GitHub carrier ✓ correct for this deployment.
3. `SyncToolDispatcher` in JS bridge — does the JS bridge use DEFAULT_TRACKER for tracker_* aliases? Memory note says JS bridge does NOT resolve tool aliases (canonical only), Java parity. Let me double check in the Dart port... n_0004: "JS bridge does NOT resolve tool aliases and does not expose alias globals". OK.
4. `teammate_job` `_postTraceComment` uses `_sourceIsGithub`, not DEFAULT_TRACKER — unaffected.

Any risk that DEFAULT_TRACKER=github breaks something in the agent session? The JS scripts in agents/ use canonical `github_*`/`jira_*` names mostly. If any script calls `tracker_*` via CLI, github routing is what we want here. Safe.

But wait — there's one more consideration: the story-dev runner also runs in NON-GitHub deployments? No — machine-kit is THIS repo's machine; its ai-teammate loop is GitHub-issues-only. The upstream dmtools-agents configs stay tracker-agnostic (ticket point 4 = upstream, later). Good — machine-kit pinning github is correct deployment-specific config. This matches the ticket: "machine-kit side first — no upstream wait".

Also note: `fa-review-kimi.json` (review) — ticket says dev + rework only. The review agent's comments go through... review posts `outputs/pr_review.json` + inline comments via gh, and its trace comments. The ticket explicitly scopes to dev + rework. I'll leave review alone but mention it in the PR description.

Hmm — actually wait. Let me reconsider adding DEFAULT_TRACKER to the runner envVariables once more. The alternative: the ai-teammate workflow step env could set DEFAULT_TRACKER=github. But workflow-level env does NOT reach PropertyReader overrides (those come from params.envVariables / dmtools.env / OS env — actually OS env DOES reach it! `propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` → getValue → resolution chain: overrides → config.properties → dmtools.env → OS environment. The workflow step env vars are OS env of the dmtools process!).

So `DEFAULT_TRACKER` could be set in `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`'s "Run agent" step env. The ticket says runners (step 2) with only cliPromptsByTracker... and step 3's parenthetical "(github when the GitHub router serves the ticket)".

Decision: put `DEFAULT_TRACKER: github` in the dev+rework runner envVariables — it's the strongest, self-contained wiring: works for workflow runs AND manual `dmtools run` of the runner.   when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must
render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###` (ATX hashes — never `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` prefixes)
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: fenced with the language tag:
  (```dart
  final reader = PropertyReader();
  ```)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: GFM pipes with a `|---|` separator row
- Task lists: `- [ ] item`

Do not use Jira wiki markup — no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no
`{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}`, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
read them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

  `cli_execute_command` and the CliAgent command phases — buffered and
  monitored — now mirror every child output line to dmtools' own stderr as
  it arrives (line-buffered, always on; no flags or env toggles) while the
  captured strings stay byte-identical for well-formed UTF-8 output
  (malformed byte sequences decode leniently to U+FFFD on both the
  buffered and monitored paths where the previous strict decode threw a
  `FormatException`; mirroring itself is best-effort — a failing stderr
  sink never aborts the capture or the batch).
  `dmtools run <config>` therefore streams the inner agent's work into the
  CI step log live, and the ai-teammate workflow drops its `FA_LOG_FILE` +
  `tail -F | sed` follower side-channel (the trace file itself stays,

### Changed

- Tracker-specific CLI prompts engage on the GitHub machine (gh-125):
  `CliAgent` now passes the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via
  `PropertyReader`, Java `configuration.getDefaultTracker()` parity) into
  `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands`, so a `cliPromptsByTracker` entry for
  the serving tracker is actually selected — previously the lookup always
  fell back to `ado` and tracker-specific prompt files were dead config.
  The dev + rework machine-kit runners (`fa-bug-dev`, `fa-story-dev`,
  `fa-rework-zai`) pin `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github` and add
  `cliPromptsByTracker.github → machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/
  github_comment_format.md`, so machine comments on GitHub issues render as
  GitHub-flavored Markdown (fenced code blocks, `##` headings, `[text](url)`
  links, GFM tables) instead of the Jira wiki markup observed on gh-122
  (`{code}` blocks, `h3.` headers). Parents in dmtools-agents stay
  tracker-agnostic — the `github` entries are this deployment's override.

## 3. The runner layer (model routing)

A **runner** is a thin child config that pins a provider on top of an agent
config from the `agents/` submodule. Everything else — instructions, lifecycle,
JS actions — is inherited from the parent.

| Runner file (machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/) | Parent (agents/) | Provider | Model | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fa-story-dev.json` | `story_development.json` | zai | glm-5.3-flash | story dev (default path) |
| `fa-bug-dev.json` | `bug_development.json` | zai | glm-5.3-flash | `[BUG]` tickets |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | `pr_review.json` | kimi | k3 | PR review (stronger reviewer model) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | `pr_rework.json` | zai | glm-5.3-flash | rework rounds |

arguments.content:
### What changed
Machine comments on GitHub issues now render as GitHub-flavored Markdown instead of Jira wiki markup: `CliAgent` passes the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via `PropertyReader`) into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands`, so `cliPromptsByTracker` entries for the serving tracker are actually selected, and the dev + rework machine-kit runners engage a new `github` prompt (Markdown comment-format rules).

### Key decisions
- Tracker lookup at the `CliAgent` level mirrors Java (`configuration.getDefaultTracker()` inside `buildCommands`) — resolveCliPrompts semantics untouched
- `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md` prescribes fenced code blocks, `##` headings, `[text](url)` links, GFM tables and bans `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` prefixes (the gh-122 leak)
- Runners pin `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github` (this loop is GitHub-issues-only) so the `github` key resolves deterministically; parents in `agents/` stay tracker-agnostic — upstream `github` entries are a later dmtools-agents PR
- Review runner untouched (posts structured PR-review output); Java's `contentOutput.target=confluence` prompt-routing is not ported (out of scope, tied to InstructionProcessor work)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart test/machine_kit/tracker_comment_format_test.dart
```

  CFG -->|cliPromptsByTracker.github| B[CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands]
  ENV --> A[CliAgent._executeCliCommands] -->|trackerType| B
  B -->|resolveCliPrompts merges| P[Combined prompt + github_comment_format.md]
  P --> CLI[fa session] --> GH[Markdown comment on GitHub issue]
```

gh-125 complete — machine comments on GitHub issues now get GitHub-flavored Markdown instead of Jira wiki markup. TDD throughout (RED confirmed before each production change).

**Changes (ticket fix steps 1–3; step 4/upstream intentionally deferred):**
1. **New instruction file** `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md` — prescribes fenced code blocks, `##`/`###` headings, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables; bans `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes (modeled on the sibling `ado_comment_format.md`).
2. **Runner wiring** (`fa-bug-dev.json`, `fa-story-dev.json`, `fa-rework-zai.json`): `params.cliPromptsByTracker.github → [the format file]` (deep-merges over the tracker-agnostic parents via the existing `_ParentConfigResolver`) **plus** `"DEFAULT_TRACKER": "github"` in envVariables — without the pin the Dart lookup falls back to `"ado"` and the github key never engages.
3. **Dart parity fix** `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`: `_executeCliCommands` now passes `trackerType: propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` into `buildCommands` (verified against fresh Java upstream: `CliCommandBuilder` uses `configuration.getDefaultTracker()` internally). Blank/unset keeps the Java `"ado"` fallback.
4. Tests (12 new): 3 lifecycle tests in `test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart` (observe the merged prompt end-to-end via a `cat` command — `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github/jira/blank`) and 9 wiring tests in `test/machine_kit/tracker_comment_format_test.dart` (format-file contract, per-runner `cliPromptsByTracker` selection resolved through the real parent chain via `RunCommandProcessor`, parents untouched, DEFAULT_TRACKER pin).
5. CHANGELOG (Unreleased → Changed) + the `docs/ai_factory.md` runner example kept accurate.

**Verification:** full suite **2707 passed, 12 skipped** (with QuickJS .so via `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`), `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, coverage **97.2%** (≥80 gate), `crap4dart check --all` 20 passed / 1 known class_size warning / 4 skipped, `crap4dart analyze` CRAP 0.00 (threshold 8).

**Notes:** review runner left out per ticket scope (posts structured PR-review output); Java's `contentOutput.target=confluence` prompt-routing (`resolvePromptTrackerType`) is not ported — recorded in memory as a deliberate gap tied to the unported InstructionProcessor work, not an oversight. gh-125 complete — machine comments on GitHub issues now get GitHub-flavored Markdown instead of Jira wiki markup. TDD throughout (RED confirmed before each production change).

**Changes (ticket fix steps 1–3; step 4/upstream intentionally deferred):**

1. **New instruction file** `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md` — prescribes fenced code blocks, `##`/`###` headings, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables; bans `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes (modeled on the sibling `ado_comment_format.md`).
2. **Runner wiring** (`fa-bug-dev.json`, `fa-story-dev.json`, `fa-rework-zai.json`): `params.cliPromptsByTracker.github → [the format file]` (deep-merges over the tracker-agnostic parents) **plus** `"DEFAULT_TRACKER": "github"` in envVariables — without the pin the Dart lookup falls back to `"ado"` and the github key never engages.
3. **Dart parity fix** `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`: `_executeCliCommands` now passes `trackerType: propertyReader.getDefaultTracker()` into `buildCommands` (verified against fresh Java upstream: `CliCommandBuilder` uses `configuration.getDefaultTracker()` internally). Blank/unset keeps the Java `"ado"` fallback.
4. **Tests (12 new)**: 3 lifecycle tests in `test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart` (observe the merged prompt end-to-end via a `cat` command — `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github/jira/blank`) and 9 wiring tests in `test/machine_kit/tracker_comment_format_test.dart` (format-file contract, per-runner `cliPromptsByTracker` selection resolved through the real parent chain via `RunCommandProcessor`, parents untouched, DEFAULT_TRACKER pin).
5. CHANGELOG (Unreleased → Changed) + `docs/ai_factory.md` runner example kept accurate.

**Verification:** full suite **2707 passed, 12 skipped** (QuickJS .so via `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`), `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, coverage **97.2%** (≥80 gate), `crap4dart check --all` 20 passed / 1 known class_size warning / 4 skipped, `crap4dart analyze` CRAP 0.00 (threshold 8).

**Notes:** review runner left out per ticket scope (posts structured PR-review output); Java's `contentOutput.target=confluence` prompt-routing (`resolvePromptTrackerType`) is not ported — recorded in project memory as a deliberate gap tied to the unported InstructionProcessor work. PR description written to `outputs/response.md`.

— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comment. - Use `#`/`##` headings, ` ``` ` code fences, `-` bullets. - Required sections: `## Issues/Notes`, `## Approach`, `## Files Modified`, `## Test Coverage`. 2. `outputs/review_replies.json` - **Mandatory** when the PR has open review threads. - If there are no open threads, write `{ "replies": [] }`. - Format: ```json { "replies": [ { "inReplyToId": 1234567890, "threadId": "", "reply": "outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md" } ] } ``` 3. `outputs/review_replies/*.md` - One Markdown file per open PR review thread. - The file path is referenced from `outputs/review_replies.json` via the `reply` field. - Keep each reply concise and factual; reference the fix location when possible. The value above is a placeholder showing *where* the field goes, not what it should look like. - Do **not** put the reply body inline in the JSON; use the `reply` field only as a file path reference. - ⚠️ **Common mistake**: `pr_discussions_raw.json` uses the field names `rootCommentId` and `body`. ## PR Description

### What changed
Machine comments on GitHub issues now render as GitHub-flavored Markdown instead of Jira wiki markup: `CliAgent` passes the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via `PropertyReader`) into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands`, so `cliPromptsByTracker` entries for the serving tracker are actually selected, and the dev + rework machine-kit runners engage a new `github` prompt (Markdown comment-format rules).

### Key decisions
- Tracker lookup at the `CliAgent` level mirrors Java (`configuration.getDefaultTracker()` inside `buildCommands`) — resolveCliPrompts semantics untouched
- `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md` prescribes fenced code blocks, `##` headings, `[text](url)` links, GFM tables and bans `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` prefixes (the gh-122 leak)
- Runners pin `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github` (this loop is GitHub-issues-only) so the `github` key resolves deterministically; parents in `agents/` stay tracker-agnostic — upstream `github` entries are a later dmtools-agents PR
- Review runner untouched (posts structured PR-review output); Java's `contentOutput.target=confluence` prompt-routing is not ported (out of scope, tied to InstructionProcessor work)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart test/machine_kit/tracker_comment_format_test.dart
```

Machine comments on GitHub issues use Jira wiki markup ({code}, h3.) — engage cliPromptsByTracker for github (markdown) + wire trackerType in CliAgent
## Summary

Machine comments on GitHub issues are posted in **Jira wiki markup** (observed on #122: 6× `{code}` blocks, 4× `h3.` headers — unreadable on GitHub). The ecosystem has a per-tracker formatting mechanism, but it is never engaged for our GitHub loop:

1. `cliPromptsByTracker` exists (`agents/intake.json`): `{"jira": [jira_markup_transform.md, jira_comment_format.md], "ado": [ado_markup_transform.md, ado_comment_format.md]}` — but **bug/story development configs don't set it at all**, and there is **no `github` key** / no `agents/instructions/tracker/github_comment_format.md` upstream.
2. The Dart port never passes `trackerType` into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands` (`lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart:249-255` calls it without the arg) — `resolveCliPrompts` then defaults to `"ado"`, so even a `github` key would never be selected. Java passes the tracker type from the job/ticket context.

## Evidence (gh-122 machine comments)

```
{code}dart
final reader = PropertyReader();
{code}
h3. Fix
```

## Fix (machine-kit side first — no upstream wait)

1. Add `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md`: markdown rules — fenced ``` blocks, `##`/`###` headers, no `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables.
2. Wire into runners `machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/fa-*.json` (dev + rework): `"cliPromptsByTracker": {"github": ["./machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md"]}` (config_merger deep-merges the map with the parent).
3. Dart parity fix: pass `trackerType` into `buildCommands`, derived from the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader — `github` when the GitHub router serves the ticket) so the `github` key resolves. (Java `CliCommandBuilder` receives the tracker from the ticket context.)
4. Upstream (dmtools-agents PR, later): add `github` entries to dev configs + share the markdown format file.

## Impact

Readability of every machine comment on GitHub issues (#122, #123, and all future runs).

{
  "key": "gh-125",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "Machine comments on GitHub issues use Jira wiki markup ({code}, h3.) — engage cliPromptsByTracker for github (markdown) + wire trackerType in CliAgent",
    "description": "## Summary

Machine comments on GitHub issues are posted in **Jira wiki markup** (observed on #122: 6× `{code}` blocks, 4× `h3.` headers — unreadable on GitHub). The ecosystem has a per-tracker formatting mechanism, but it is never engaged for our GitHub loop:

1. `cliPromptsByTracker` exists (`agents/intake.json`): `{"jira": [jira_markup_transform.md, jira_comment_format.md], "ado": [ado_markup_transform.md, ado_comment_format.md]}` — but **bug/story development configs don't set it at all**, and there is **no `github` key** / no `agents/instructions/tracker/github_comment_format.md` upstream.
2. The Dart port never passes `trackerType` into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands` (`lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart:249-255` calls it without the arg) — `resolveCliPrompts` then defaults to `"ado"`, so even a `github` key would never be selected. Java passes the tracker type from the job/ticket context.

## Evidence (gh-122 machine comments)

```
{code}dart
final reader = PropertyReader();
{code}
h3. Fix
```

## Fix (machine-kit side first — no upstream wait)

1. Add `machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md`: markdown rules — fenced ``` blocks, `##`/`###` headers, no `{code}`/`{panel}`/`h1.` Jira prefixes, `[text](url)` links, `|---|` tables.
2. Wire into runners `machine-kit/teammate-install/runners/fa-*.json` (dev + rework): `"cliPromptsByTracker": {"github": ["./machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/github_comment_format.md"]}` (config_merger deep-merges the map with the parent).
3. Dart parity fix: pass `trackerType` into `buildCommands`, derived from the active tracker (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` via PropertyReader — `github` when the GitHub router serves the ticket) so the `github` key resolves. (Java `CliCommandBuilder` receives the tracker from the ticket context.)
4. Upstream (dmtools-agents PR, later): add `github` entries to dev configs + share the markdown format file.

## Impact

Readability of every machine comment on GitHub issues (#122, #123, and all future runs)."
  }
}

## Refined scope (after tracing the actual comment source)

The `{code}` / `h3.` markup is **NOT LLM output** — it comes from hard-coded Jira-wiki templates in dmtools-agents post-actions (`developBugAndCreatePR.js:98,124,140,169,279`, `preparePRForReview.js`, etc.). Upstream fix goes via a separate PR there (tracker-aware templates). 

**This issue = the Dart side that makes ALL such comments readable on GitHub regardless of upstream:**

1. **Jira-markup → markdown converter in the comment path of the JS bridge**: when `jira_post_comment` / `tracker` comment tools route to GitHub Issues (`lib/src/js/sync_tools/tracker_github_router.dart`, `_postComment`), convert the body: 
   - `{code:lang}` / `{code}` → fenced ``` blocks
   - `h1.`–`h6.` → `#`–`######`
   - `[text|url]` → `[text](url)`
   - `*bold*` → `**bold**` (Jira bold vs md italic)
   - `{panel:title=X}` → `> **X**` blockquote (optional)
   - `{color:...}{color}` → strip
   Java-parity note: the Jira path must pass bodies through unchanged — conversion applies only in the GitHub router.
2. **Wire `trackerType` into `CliCommandBuilder.buildCommands`** (see original body) so `cliPromptsByTracker["github"]` can resolve.
3. **machine-kit**: `github_comment_format.md` + `"github"` key in runners (for LLM-generated text).
4. Tests: converter unit tests (each construct), router test (comment round-trip), builder test (trackerType selection).

# gh-125 Rework — Jira-markup → Markdown converter in the GitHub comment path

## Issues/Notes

- The owner refined the scope on the ticket *after* the original dev run: the `{code}` / `h3.` markup on gh-122 is **not LLM output** — it is hard-coded Jira-wiki template text in the dmtools-agents JS post-actions (`developBugAndCreatePR.js`, `preparePRForReview.js`, …). The PR's prompt-file fix alone therefore cannot make those comments readable.
- Refined-scope item 1 (converter in the JS-bridge comment path) and item 4 (converter/router/builder tests) were missing from the PR; items 2 (`trackerType` in `buildCommands`) and 3 (machine-kit `github_comment_format.md` + runner wiring) were already implemented.
- No CI failures, merge conflicts, or open review threads on the PR (0 reviews / 0 inline comments — hence an empty `review_replies.json`).
- Not done (deliberately): upstream template fix in dmtools-agents (separate upstream PR per the owner's comment); `{quote}` and `{color}`-content heuristics beyond tag stripping were not requested.

## Approach

- New pure converter `jiraMarkupToMarkdown` (`lib/src/js/sync_tools/jira_markup.dart`), wired into the ONE comment path that serves GitHub Issues: `TrackerGitHubRouter._postComment`. Every construct from the refined scope:
  - `{code:lang}` / `{code}lang` / `{code}` paired blocks → fenced ``` blocks (all three spellings seen in the wild, incl. the gh-122 `{code}dart` form); a single-line pair spanning the whole line becomes a fence, a pair embedded after text becomes an inline backtick span (a mid-line fence would not open a GFM block, and a lone trailing fence would swallow the rest of the comment); an unclosed block gets a defensive closing fence.
  - `h1.`–`h6.` → `#`–`######`; `[text|url]` → `[text](url)`; `*bold*` → `**bold**` with lookaround guards so existing `**bold**`, `-`/`*` bullets and `2 * 3 * 4` arithmetic never match; `{panel:title=X}` … `{panel}` → blockquote; `{color:…}` tags stripped.
- Java-parity guarantee: the Jira path is untouched — the converter is imported only by the GitHub router, so Jira-routed bodies pass through byte-for-byte.
- TDD: the converter tests, the router round-trip test and the builder-level github-selection test were all written first; the router test reproduced the exact bug (body posted verbatim as `h3. Done\n{code}…`).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/jira_markup.dart` — new converter (stateful line scanner: code state → panel state → inline pairs → link/bold).
- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/tracker_github_router.dart` — `_postComment` converts the body via `jiraMarkupToMarkdown` before POSTing.
- `test/js/sync_tools/jira_markup_test.dart` — new, 28 tests (every construct + passthrough + gh-122 evidence end-to-end).
- `test/js/sync_tools/tracker_github_router_test.dart` — new fixture round-trip: routed `jira_post_comment` posts Markdown to `/repos/o/r/issues/50/comments`.
- `test/agents/cli_agent_tracker_prompts_test.dart` — new: `DEFAULT_TRACKER=github|jira|blank` selects the matching `cliPromptsByTracker` prompts end-to-end (moved here from `cli_agent_test.dart` to keep that file under the 800-line gate).
- `test/agents/cli_agent_test.dart` — builder-level `resolveCliPrompts('github')` selection test.
- `crap4dart` gate refactors (gates are law): converter split into a small `_Converter` state machine (was CC 19 / 65 lines), tests split into group functions.

## Test Coverage

- Focused: 28 converter tests + router fixture suite (46) + agents suite (226) — all green.
- Full loop: **2737 tests passed, 12 skipped** (integration-tagged), `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, coverage **97.1 %** (≥ 80 % gate), `crap4dart check --all` **20 passed / 1 warned** (the pre-existing Java-parity `class_size` exemption) / 4 skipped, `crap4dart analyze` CRAP 8.00 (threshold 8.0).
- Router round-trip proof: `jira_post_comment` with the gh-122-shaped body now POSTs `### Done` / fenced `dart` block / `[PR #1](https://x.y/1)` to the GitHub API.

Rework complete. Summary of what was done and why:

## The rework driver
The input contained no CI failures, conflicts, or review threads — the actionable finding was the **owner's scope refinement** posted on ticket gh-125 after the original dev run: the `{code}`/`h3.` markup on gh-122 comes from **hard-coded Jira-wiki templates** in the agents' JS post-actions (`developBugAndCreatePR.js`, `preparePRForReview.js`), *not* LLM output. So the PR's prompt-file fix alone couldn't make those comments readable — refined-scope item 1 (a Jira-markup→Markdown converter in the GitHub comment router) was missing, and the rework implements it.

## What changed (TDD — RED verified before every fix)
1. **`lib/src/js/sync_tools/jira_markup.dart`** (new) — `jiraMarkupToMarkdown`: stateful line-scanner converting `{code:lang}`/`{code}lang`/`{code}` paired blocks → fenced blocks (incl. the exact gh-122 `{code}dart` form; an unclosed block gets a defensive fence), `h1.`–`h6.` → ATX headings, `[text|url]` → `[text](url)`, `*bold*` → `**bold**` (lookaround guards protect existing `**bold**`, bullets, arithmetic), `{panel:title=X}` → blockquote, `{color}` stripped. Design nuances the tests forced out: a `{code}` pair embedded after text becomes a **backtick span**, not a fence (a mid-line ``` never opens a GFM block; a lone trailing fence would swallow the rest of the comment); code-block content passes through verbatim.
2. **`TrackerGitHubRouter._postComment`** — converts the body before POSTing. **Java parity**: the converter is imported *only* by the GitHub router — Jira-routed bodies stay byte-for-byte.
3. **Tests** (30 new): 28 converter unit tests (every refined-scope construct + passthrough + gh-122 evidence end-to-end), a router fixture round-trip proving routed `jira_post_comment` POSTs Markdown, and a builder-level `resolveCliPrompts('github')` selection test.
